segments.text: Afternoon, both of you. Thanks for making the time between consults. Before we start, I'd like to confirm what we agreed by email. I'm using this meeting's transcript to write up your requirements, and the AI that helps me with that runs on my own laptop, so nothing goes to an outside service.
Are you both still okay with that?
Yes, that's fine with me.
Yeah, no problem. Thank you. Hennie, are you at the Centurion Clinic today?
I am, yes. Sorry about the noise. There's a Great Dane in the waiting room who does not want his injection.
He's been complaining since one o'clock. Shame. Poor thing. Okay, so to start, can you walk me through how bookings work today, from the moment someone wants an appointment?

So they phone. All three clinics, Centurion, Irene, and Oli van Houtbosch, have their own landline and their own paper diary at reception. The receptionist finds a gap, writes the pet's name and the owner's number in pencil, and that's it. And the practice software.
I saw VetDesk on your invoice.

VetDesk Pro, yes. That's where all the clinical records live. The owner's details, vaccination history, billing. But it has no proper diary. We tried its calendar years ago, and the receptionists hated it, so the paper diary came back.
What goes wrong with the phones and the diary?

Mornings are the worst. Between 8 and 10, the phones just don't stop. And there's one receptionist per clinic who is also checking people in and taking payments. We miss a lot of calls. And people get double-booked because someone rubbed out a booking and someone else wrote over it.
And no-shows. We have maybe 20 no-shows a week across the three clinics. Each one is a 30-minute slot gone.
So if I'm hearing you right, the goals are fewer missed calls, no double bookings, and fewer no-shows.
That's it. If I had to pick one, it's the phones. My receptionists are burning out.
Okay. Roughly how many appointments do you book in a day? All three together. Across all three, I'd say about 120 a
day. And does that change through the year?
Hugely. Annual vaccinations bunch up in February and March because so many of our clients got their puppies at Christmas. And then there's the rabies drive in March as well. It easily doubles then.
Noted. So, what would the new system have to do? Imagine it's working well. What does a pet owner do? They go onto a website on their phone, pick the
clinic, pick what it's for, a vaccination, a check-up, a sick pet, and see the open times. They choose one and it's booked. And then they get a reminder the day before.

And the vaccination reminders. Vet Desk knows when each animal is due. Right now Charmaine prints a list every month and the girls phone people. If that could go out automatically with a link to book, that's half the work gone.

That makes sense. And on the reception side, they need to see the day for their clinic, move bookings around, and put in phone bookings too, because some of our older clients will never book online. So the phones would stay, but everything goes into one diary instead of paper.
Yes, the paper diary goes. That we've decided. The phones stay, but the paper goes.
Good. Should
owners be able to choose a specific vet? Some would want to. Dr. Makona at Irene has her regulars, but it
mustn't be required. And emergencies. Should a sick animal be bookable online?

Hum. That's a good question. I don't want someone booking a slot for tomorrow at 11 for a dog that's been hit by a car. But a cat that's been vomiting, maybe. I need to talk to the other vets about where we draw that line.
I'll put that down as open. What about the reminders? SMS or WhatsApp?
I think most of our clients would rather get WhatsApp than SMS. That's my feeling from the front desk. Anyway, we'd need to check. Maybe ask people in the waiting room for a week.
We do already pay for an SMS bundle through VetDesk for the account statements.
Okay. Now the phone numbers. You mentioned Popia in your email.

Yes. Our attorney went through it with us last year. Owners' phone numbers are personal information. We may use them for their pets' appointments and reminders, but nothing else, no marketing, and we may not hand them to another company to use for its own purposes.
And every client signs the consent bid on the registration form, but that's on paper too, in a file at

each clinic. Then, whatever we build has to record that consent itself, and anyone who books online has to agree before we send them anything. And the company that sends the messages would be an operator under Popia, so you'd need a written agreement with them.
Agreed. That has to be in from day one.
One thing I'd suggest for the no-shows, ask for a small deposit, say a hundred rand, when someone books online for a Saturday, and refund it when they arrive.
I see the point, but I'm not sure our clients will like it. Let me talk to the partners before we decide anything.

Sorry, can I go back to the numbers? I've just opened last week's diaries. It's more like a hundred and sixty a day. I forgot that Oli van Houtbosch does a full Saturday morning now, and Centurion has two vets, not
one. Thanks, that's helpful. So a hundred and sixty on a normal day, doubling in vaccination season.
That sounds right.
Would you want owners to see their pet's medical history online while they're there? Some practices do that.
No, definitely not, not in this project. The vets don't want owners reading clinical notes without someone explaining them. Bookings and reminders only.
Understood. Let's talk about VetDesk. Can it share its data with another system?
There is an API. Our rep mentioned it at a conference.
But they charge for it per clinic, and when the Pretoria East practice asked for it, it took VetDesk three months
to switch it on. Then that's a risk to the timeline. I'd ask them for the price and a date in writing as soon as possible. When do you need this working?
Before vaccination season. So live by the first of February at the latest.
Ideally mid-January, so the girls have two weeks to get used to it before the rush. And the budget?
We've put aside 180,000 rand to build it. And the running costs, the messages, and the hosting must stay under 2,500 a month for all three clinics. That's my limit.
Clear. And how should it look? Any preferences? A green. The logo green.
I don't want that.

Great. Is there anything you'd want later, but not in the first version? Ordering pet food online and paying for it, maybe. Next year. Okay. I'll send a summary with the open questions tomorrow morning. Thank you both, and good luck with the Great Dane.
you
